newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water says trading ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water says trading ahead of budget.

text.p: British water and sewerage firm Thames Water Plc said on Tuesday that trading was ahead of budget and expected to continue showing strength.
"Thames has made an excellent start to the year, trading ahead of budget and...this strong performance is expected to continue," chairman Sir Robert Clarke told the annual meeting.
Clarke said the company's non-regulated businesses were "now earning good profits," with international activities in particular making good progress.
He confirmed there would be no restrictions on water use in the area during this summer, despite a period of prolonged drought during Britain's driest period for 200 years.
Clarke said leaks from the company's pipes alone were running at around 20 percent of supplies and that Thames would continue to put cutting leaks as its priority.
Thames saw around 38 percent of supplies leak out of all pipes, including those which connect to households, during 1995-96.

Clarke said the company's 230 million stg liability under the new Labour government's one-off tax on excess profits would be met by borrowings, so that customers' bills would not be affected "in the short term."
The government announced the tax, aimed at raising a total 5.2 billion stg, in its first budget on July 2.
